name: Curator
description: Asks an LLM what your library has in common and builds the answers into ordered playlists surfaced as home screen rows.
overview: LLM-inferred vibe categories for your Jellyfin library.

versions.changelog: Batch size 0 now sends the whole library in one request, and is the default: a thread running through items split across two batches is one the model never gets to see. The settings page is reorganised into four tabs by subject — Model, Library, Categories, Home screen — with the Anthropic Batch API alongside the model it belongs to. Items in collections you name, Oscar Nominees and Oscar Winners by default, now reach the model labelled, to be weighed as evidence rather than filed under. Adds a playlist reconcile button that rebuilds lost playlists, removes empty categories and deletes orphaned playlists without calling a model, and the category cap now spends empty categories before live ones. The expanded detail panels have been rebuilt for narrow dashboard columns. Requires Jellyfin 10.11.11 or newer.

Stops items orphaned by a removed or remounted library folder reaching the model. Jellyfin keeps the database row when a library folder goes away, so it still looks like a real item and plays back as nothing; on one server 36 of 298 items were such ghosts and were landing in real playlists. Home screen rows are now created enabled and asking for one item rather than switched off at zero, and rows written incorrectly by an earlier version are repaired on the next run. Adds a run history list under the generate button with per-run details and a cost breakdown, and a button that re-syncs home screen rows without an LLM call. Requires Jellyfin 10.11.11 or newer.

Adds a progress panel to the configuration page. Starting a run used to replace the status line with a note telling you to go read the server log; a run takes minutes and costs money, so it now shows a progress bar, the phase in plain words, and a stacked breakdown of estimated cost into input and output with token, call and cache counts. Cost reads as not priced rather than zero when no prices are set, and sub-cent totals show as less than a cent rather than rounding to nothing. Requires Jellyfin 10.11.11 or newer.

Fixes personalization for anyone who watches television. Jellyfin records playback against episodes, so a series row carries no watch history and every TV viewer read as a viewer of nothing — measured on a 297-item library, six users' activity held 210 movie entries against 3 series entries. Episode playback is now rolled up onto the series and reaches the model as watch depth. Shared categories go to every user rather than being opted into. A run interrupted by a plugin install is now reported as what it is instead of a stack trace. The landscape/portrait row split is a setting, and both category pools default to a floor of 4 members and a cap of 10. Requires Jellyfin 10.11.11 or newer.

Adds native Google Gemini and xAI Grok providers, both constraining the model to a response schema so a malformed answer cannot lose a batch. Every run now writes a complete JSON record — settings, every step, every prompt and response, and cost per call and per run. Category size and count limits are told to the model as well as enforced on its answer, and a renamed category keeps its playlist and home screen row instead of being rebuilt. Over-cap categories are pruned oldest-first, and deleting a category now removes its playlists. Requires Jellyfin 10.11.11 or newer.

Fixes the 10.11.11 ABI break that made every run fail, plus the two model-response bugs that discarded results. Adds prompt caching, an optional batch API path, a tabbed configuration page with category management, and a tag limit. Requires Jellyfin 10.11.11 or newer.

Feature-complete pipeline: library scan, LLM providers (Anthropic / OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible), category reconciliation, playlist building with ownership tagging, home screen rows via Collection Sections, a weekly scheduled task, and a full configuration page with a manual run button. Not yet exercised against a live server - please report issues.
